Updated — the same screen at **[http://maker:4001](http://maker:4001)** now has both changes. Please try these two actions:

👉 **1. Save a link from a well-known site** (e.g. `https://github.com`). Notice it now shows the **site's own small icon** and a **preview image** for the page, instead of just a letter.

👉 **2. Now paste that exact same link again and press Save.** Instead of creating a duplicate, the app should **jump to and highlight the one you already saved**, with a little message telling you it's already there.

A few things I decided that I'd like you to check:
- **Preview image only "when available":** I show a preview for pages that have one, and simply leave it off for pages that don't — so if you save a plain/obscure link, you'll see the icon but no preview banner. Try saving something like `https://example.com` to see that difference. Is "show it when it exists, skip it quietly when it doesn't" the right call?
- **The small site icon** loads from the real site. If a site doesn't provide one (or it can't load), it **falls back to the letter badge** so the item never looks broken.
- **What counts as "the same link":** I treat `github.com` and `github.com/` (and the `www.` version) as the *same* bookmark, so trailing slashes don't trick it into a duplicate. Does that match your expectation?

One note: when you paste a duplicate, the app brings up the existing bookmark and tells you it's there — the **actual editing/updating of it is the very next flow we'll build**, so for now it just surfaces it. 

Does the saving flow now match what you had in mind?
